NOTICE.TITLE: Regulation (EU) 2024/444 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 12 February 2024 on know-your-customer requirements for virtual asset service providers
NOTICE.CONTENTS:
Article 1 - Subject matter. This Regulation establishes specific know-your-customer (KYC) obligations for virtual asset service providers (VASPs) registered or operating within the Union, supplementing the general requirements of Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843.
Article 2 - Definitions. For the purposes of this Regulation: (a) 'virtual asset' means a digital representation of value that can be digitally traded or transferred and can be used for payment or investment purposes, as defined in the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendations; (b) 'virtual asset service provider' means any natural or legal person who provides one or more virtual asset services on a professional basis; (c) 'travel rule' means the requirement under FATF Recommendation 16 to obtain, hold and transmit originator and beneficiary information during virtual asset transfers.
Article 3 - Customer identification for virtual asset transactions. 1. VASPs shall perform customer identification and verification before establishing a business relationship or executing any virtual asset transfer exceeding EUR 1,000. 2. For unhosted wallet transfers exceeding EUR 1,000, VASPs shall: (a) collect the name and address of the unhosted wallet owner; (b) verify the customer's ownership of the unhosted wallet using a cryptographic signature or small test transaction; (c) retain records of the verification process for five years.
Article 4 - Travel rule compliance. 1. VASPs shall ensure that virtual asset transfers are accompanied by originator and beneficiary information as specified in Annex I. 2. For transfers below EUR 1,000 to unhosted wallets, VASPs shall collect and retain originator information but need not verify the beneficiary's identity unless risk indicators are present.
Article 5 - Enhanced monitoring for high-risk jurisdictions. Transfers to or from addresses associated with jurisdictions on the FATF high-risk list shall be subject to enhanced scrutiny, including manual review by a compliance officer prior to execution.
Article 6 - Sanctions screening. VASPs shall screen all customers and counterparties against the EU Consolidated Sanctions List maintained by the OFAC and the UN Security Council Consolidated List before executing any transfer.
Article 7 - Record keeping. All KYC records, transaction records, and compliance correspondence shall be retained for a minimum period of five years and made available to competent authorities upon request within 48 hours.
Article 8 - Reporting to FIU. VASPs shall file suspicious activity reports (SARs) with the national FIU within 24 hours of identifying a suspicious transaction. Reports shall use the standardised format published by Eurostat.
Article 9 - Supervisory fees. VASPs registered under this Regulation shall contribute to a supervisory fund administered by ESMA. Annual fees are calculated on the basis of average daily transaction volume as specified in Annex II.
Article 10 - Entry into force. This Regulation shall enter into force on 1 August 2024.
